text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Despite claims by rival investment bankers that Macquarie Bank's chances of being selected for the role of advising the federal government on the Telstra privatisation have been damaged by the charges laid against senior executive Simon Hannes, the head of Macquarie's corporate advisory division, Alistair Lucas, says he doesn't believe the charges will affect anyone's willingness to deal with the bank. Page 1.

Optus has launched a High Court bid to challenge an Austel ruling that would have allowed Telstra to offer big discounts to certain customers in the A$4 billion international calls market. Optus legal director Robert Simpson said the company is concerned Telstra will anti-competitively target Optus customers and customers of other service providers. Page 1. --

Coal & Allied Industries Ltd has made an application to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission under new provisions in the Workplace Relations Act to order three unions and their members at its Hunter Valley mine to cease all industrial action immdiately and not to engage in any further industrial action. Page 3.

After obtaining only meagre price rises for some categories of iron ore, BHP has been accused of rushing negotiations with Japanese steel mills in much the same way as the recent coal settlements. However, BHP Iron Ore spokeswoman Judith Thomson said the company was happy with the result, considering that Japanese steel output is forecast to contract by about one million tonnes for the next fiscal year. Page 15.

With the federal government's deadline for bids from brokers to participate in the A$10 billion privatisation of Telstra closing on Monday, some brokers suggested yesterday that County NatWest and SBC Warburg should be ruled out of the Telstra float becaue of conflicting interests with Optus. Page 15.

The chief executive of South Africa's Plessey Corp Ltd, John Temple, says he will spend no more than one year trying to make a profit from the three divisions Plessey acquired from AWA Ltd. If successful, Temple hinted at a possible public float of the operations by 1999. Page 15.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the lead of the United States Federal Communications Commission, which raised US$20 billion last year through auctioning the radio communications spectrum, Australia's Spectrum Management Agency will next month commence a two-stage auction of airwaves. The first auction will sell licences for the 500MHz frequency and is expected to raise about A$5 million. The second auction of the 1800MHz frequency later this year is expected to raise between A$1 billion and A$2.5 billion. Page 31.

Touted as a possible successor to Foster's Brewing Group Ltd chief executive Ted Kunkel, senior vice-president of strategy and development, Keith Lambert, has announced his amicable resignation from Foster's to take up a position at the Rosemount wine business. Page 31.

In an acceleration of its international expansion plans, Lend Lease Corp Ltd has announced a deal to help develop a A$1 billion commercial and residential development in northern Bangkok in partnership with Thailand's Modern Home Development Public Co Ltd. Page 31.

United States-based cable companies have hit Australia's regional pay TV and telephony market. Los Angeles-based Northgate Communications is set to switch on its pay TV service in Ballarat after spending A$20 million laying cable and plans to cable Wagga Wagga next. Page 31.

Publishing and Broadcasting has appointed media consultant and Optus Communications board member Peter O'Connell as a director of its investment division, PBL Enterprises. O'Connell will handle investments in gaming and telecoms, including Sky Channel, Matrix Telecommunications and the Sydney Casino. Page 33.

In a deal that would give Reef Casino Trust Ltd valuable time to negotiate with bankers and stave off receivers, Casinos Austria International Ltd - operator of the Reef Casino and 13 percent shareholder in the trust - is considering the payment of a A$3 million rent commitment. Page 33.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Amid speculation that the three airports in the government's first round of airport sales -- Perth, Melbourne and Brisbane -- could fetch prices as high as A$1.35 billion for Brisbane airport, some bidders have raised concerns that the future of the airports could be jeopardised because of their heavy debt burden. Page 25.

Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting has appointed former corporate lawyer and merchant banker Peter O'Connell to head up its new gambling and telecommunications operations. O'Connell will quit his position on the board of Optus Communications and his role as Bell South's South Australian representative. Page 25.

Ending negotiations with Japanese steel mills, BHP has accepted only modest price increases for some grades of iron ore and no change for other grades or the overall volume. Under the deal, lower priced iron ore fines produced from BHP's Mt Newman mines in Western Australia will receive a 1.1 percent increase to 29.10 U.S. cents tonne, but lump ore will be priced at last year's 37.68 a tonne Page 25.

Despite announcing its participation in a A$1 billion joint venture project in Thailand with listed property developer Modern Home Development, Lend Lease Corporation's shares slipped 87 cents yesterday to A$23.17. According to analysts, the slide reflects caution in the market about risks in Lend Lease's development projects. Page 27.

As St George Bank's share price rose 10 cents yesterday to the level required for Advance shareholders to receive the full A$2.65 billion takeover price from St George, the bank announced the first of its executive appointments. The key roles of heading reasury and finance have been filled by St George personnel, but the position of head of retail banking has been won by an Advance manager. Page 27.

While George Weston Foods has raised about A$20 million through the introduction of its dividend reinvestment plan, deputy chairman and chief executive John Pascoe told shareholders yesterday that conditions in the biscuit, milling and baking industries had not improved dramatically in the past few months. Page 27.
THE AGE

While BHP claimed its negotiations with Japanese steel mills produced a satisfactory result, some industry insiders criticised the deal, claiming an improving outlook for the Japanese economy had positive implications for steel demand. BHP will receive an increase of just over one percent per dry tonne unit and lump ore will be sold at 37.68 U.S. cents, unchanged from last year. Page C1.

An anonymous fax tipped off the Australian Securities Commission and the Australian Stock Exchange to unusual trading in TNT options ahead of the October 2 bid for TNT by Dutch group KPN. According to the fax, a series of payments made by one trader for otions were paid for with a series of bank cheques, nine for A$9000 and one for A$9900. Page C1.

Lend Lease announced yesterday that it has committed about A$100 million to a A$1 billion urban renewal joint venture in Thailand with the listed Thai property development company Modern Home Development. Lend Lease will own 50 percent of the joint veture and initially contribute A$19 million. Page C1.

Concerned that Hungary is already subsidising exports above its World Trade Organisation agreement and plans to expand subsidies to more than 300 agricultural items, Australia, the United States, New Zealand and Argentina will ask the WTO to act against Hungary. Page C2.

In its quarterly report, Ashton Mining predicted improved sales in 1997 following a five percent increase in production to 41.99 million carats by the Argyle Diamond Mines joint venture. Ashton said the higher production reflected increased plant througput. Page C3.

Because of lower commodity prices and losses incurred due to a strengthening dollar, WMC yesterday reported falling revenues for the first half of 1996/97. Oil brought WMC's most significant fall in production, from 2.4 million barrels to 1.4 million, while copper production was affected by site works for the expansion of the Olympic Dam in South Australia. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
